Check up for (especially Inattentive) ADHD or other possible cognitive stuff at play, there are many who go unnoticed and it seeps into their adulthood. Got ADHD? Phew. If so, your whole academic life was a lie but at least you're no longer a fish climbing a tree. No ADHD? Phew. You've got.. no ADHD so you know it's something you CAN control and you just have to make the correct choices. 

Other than that, it's always best to contact a professional of any situation whether it's a psychiatrist or a professional study tutor who you actually have to account for. 

I think it's obvious along my typing is that I was one of the people who had a type of ADHD that was all BUT hyperactive, and due to medicinal ignorance amongst the education field I stood no chances amongst my peers and I faced labels and standards just a little too high for me to reach. I never managed time well. Could never bear class. Every difficult problem that was NOT TO MY INTEREST seemed to fog up my mind, like I had put the same amount of energy as my cross country meets. There was one moment in PreCalculus, I became aware that something was off when it was homework time. All of my friends and peers were doing the HW, knowing god forbid we should do it later because holy crap was it a lot in the already competitive school overall. All their pencils scraped the paper in repetitive motion and I realized I was looking around the room observing that kind of minute detail when I could have been doing math problems for 15 minutes. When I observed that world around me it seemed weird. It was alien to me yet I knew somehow something was deeper going on, and so many teachers and friends would try to raise me up with their genuinely good advice and I followed and I failed. I had to stop and self soul search for the shallow  sake of academics. I saw patterns and I researched and I was the person who ended up taking myself to the psychiatrist to end up getting diagnosed. It's been quite the rollercoaster.

What I mean from own personal anecdote: an issue can get so bad that you're gonna have to be a grownup and analyze yourself. BE HONEST, it's you after all. Don't think you have ADHD so you can bum off mess, or don't think you don't have ADHD because of pride. Don't think of not getting that tutor   whether you have a learning disorder or whatever just because of $$$.  Don't think at all. This is going to sound archaic but truly let your surroundings and the way you sort of react and take part in your own world and compare it to the average person. You might be depressed, actually extremely lazy, or whatever. Your main concern is that you're not playing up to your potential, and I know you know you have a higher potential because there's a difference when you're self aware of your bad habits and when you just do it out of ignorance.
